current.text: OKC traded him to Atlanta this offseason, along with Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins. The moves were mostly financial.
He is expected to come off the bench as Atlanta's sixth man and get the most bench minutes. He should mostly be staggered with Dyson Daniels for spacing, and should play more than Aaron Wiggins.

If he starts, it would most likely be in place of CJ McCollum, not Nickeil Alexander-Walker. The experts do not expect him to start over McCollum. Lloyd says starting him over Daniels would be a mistake because Dort is the worse defender and the worse offensive player.
He could lose minutes, or be traded again, if Daniels makes him expendable.
He was not a top 280 player last season.
He is only worth considering in leagues with 16 or more teams. Lloyd mentions him as a late swing pick but does not believe in it.
Lloyd expects Atlanta to use a 10-man rotation with a deep bench. That limits the minutes available to reserves.
Atlanta's playoff schedule is 4-4-3 games for a season ending March 28. The team has 14 back-to-backs, and resting players is not a concern.

durable.text: He is a wing defender who is very good at switching onto bigger forwards.
His three-point shooting swings from season to season, but he is not afraid to shoot.

note: Dort is not a draft target in our 12-team league. Yahoo ranks him 230 and ESPN 162, both sites value him at 0 USD, and the experts call him a deep-league option only. He projects for about 2.1 threes with few turnovers, but a 41.6% FG and low points and assists cost too much as a sixth man. Early in the season, check whether he starts in place of McCollum or gets heavy minutes after a guard injury. Only then is he worth a waiver look.
